differences: Scope: this is a broad review of the Blender-authored character assets and sampled deformation poses, not acceptance of runtime shading, real-time motion cadence, blending, or gameplay presentation.

Compared with the round-six archive, removing the extra eye layer resolves the conspicuous concentric/button-like appearance. The simpler dark eyes, shorter lower head, and compact cream muzzle now form a coherent friendly face while preserving the user's approved fuller limbs.

The otter tail reads as a short taper and the beaver tail as a thin paddle in rear, below, and side views; neither reads as an extra arm. Their softer roots and the rounder beaver paddle improve continuity without making the beaver bulky.
The beaver crosshatching is very subdued at the supplied view sizes. This is a minor remaining difference from the more visible reference pattern, not a silhouette failure.

The lineup retains readable cap numbers, covered ears, simple single-volume paws, and clean glove/fin attachments. Small shoulder-to-torso contour changes remain visible in close views, but there is no new pinched or disconnected-looking joint.

Across all eight beaver dive frames, the head leads and the trunk/hips/tail participate in the later poses without obvious facial distortion, cuff separation, or major equipment collision. All eight otter swim frames retain a continuous body contour through the sampled kick phases.

The eight-frame sets verify sampled pose progression and visible deformation, not continuous timing, interpolation quality, or runtime responsiveness. Fur sway in moving water and appearance from the actual gameplay camera remain unverified.
suggestions: Preserve the current head, eye, limb, paw, cap, and tail design as the asset candidate; avoid further broad proportion changes before inspecting it in the actual renderer.
Keep the beaver tail pattern restrained. Adjust its contrast only if actual gameplay-distance testing shows that the paddle needs additional definition.
Proceed to authorized runtime shade, continuous-motion, and gameplay-camera checks. The overall goal must remain pending until that evidence is reviewed.
reasoning: The authored assets now meet the soft, readable, playful character direction without a critical visible silhouette or equipment defect in the supplied views, so this asset-only checkpoint clears 90. The overall goal is still unverified because Blender stills and sparse pose samples cannot establish the final Three.js appearance or motion quality.
